description:
# AI credentials: explicit no-auth and canonical authentication mode

## Status and goal

User-approved implementation plan, based on the user-agreed behavior and read-only inspection of worktree `fix/ai-cred-no-auth-migration` (`merry-iguana`). No application changes or validation runs have been performed for this plan.

Make **No authentication** selectable in Auth Credentials and AI Credentials. Auth Credentials own the persisted authentication mode; changing it through an AI Credential updates the existing associated Auth Credential. Migrate legacy API-key-mode AI entries with empty keys into canonical no-auth credentials.

After migration, AI `metadata["auth_kind"]` is neither a runtime input nor a second source of truth. Legacy interpretation is confined to migration/rollback code. Canonical `connect_credentials.auth_kind == "none"` remains supported.

## Confirmed current behavior

- `lib/zaq/engine/connect/credential.ex` already supports `api_key`, `oauth2`, `jwt_bearer`, and `none`. No-auth requires disabled personal policy, configuration binding, and secret-free configuration.
- `lib/zaq/engine/connect/mutations.ex` provides transactional configuration/grant mutation and rejects auth changes with incompatible active personal grants.
- `lib/zaq/system/ai_provider_credential_configuration.ex` maps AI writes to `Connect.save_credential_configuration/4`, but derives explicit modes from AI metadata and can retain an existing mode when a form merely removes metadata.
- `lib/zaq/system/ai_provider_credential_migration.ex` rejects missing keys without an explicit no-auth marker, and rejects successfully decrypted blank keys.
- `priv/repo/migrations/20260918131000_backfill_connect_backed_ai_credentials.exs` independently derives mode and binding from legacy metadata. Merely relaxing preflight would leave incorrect backfill behavior.
- The AI form offers API key/OAuth2; the shared Auth Credential form offers API key/OAuth2/JWT bearer. Neither exposes no-auth.
- AI list labels, form selection, and OAuth initiation inspect AI metadata. System list/get currently return AI rows without projecting canonical authentication mode.
- Other AI writers include `lib/zaq/user_portal/provisioner.ex`; these must adopt the explicit contract too.
- Existing tracking overlaps include `zaq-jrg.23`–`.26`, `zaq-jrg.28`, and completed `zaq-p9l.4`/`.5`. Reconcile these before opening implementation issues rather than duplicating their scope or reopening completed work blindly.

## Target contract

### Ownership and request shape

1. Persist authentication mode exclusively on the associated Connect credential. Keep AI name/provider/endpoint/sovereignty and unrelated metadata in System.
2. Use explicit top-level `auth_kind` in the AI configuration request, with string/atom-key normalization at the existing boundary. A virtual AI schema field can carry form state and canonical read projection; do not add another persisted auth-mode column.
3. AI supports `api_key`, `oauth2`, and `none`. Generic Auth Credentials retain `jwt_bearer` as well.
4. An explicit valid mode wins. On update, omission preserves the freshly loaded canonical mode. On creation, omission may retain the existing API-key default, but must never infer no-auth from missing credentials.
5. Unknown modes fail validation. AI metadata cannot select or override mode. Strip the obsolete discriminator from ongoing AI writes after converting all supported callers.
6. Canonical reads drive mode labels, controls, OAuth eligibility, and runtime resolution. Missing/unavailable canonical data yields an explicit unavailable/error state rather than a guessed API-key/no-auth mode.
7. Preserve provider constraints, including OpenAI Codex's OAuth requirement. Enforce linked-AI compatibility at the shared domain mutation boundary so generic Auth Credential edits cannot put a linked AI entry into JWT bearer or an invalid provider/mode combination. Use a focused association query/validation, not a Connect → System write → Connect recursion.

### Transition behavior

| Operation | Required result |
| --- | --- |
| Create no-auth | Canonical `none`, disabled personal policy, configuration binding, no secret fields or global grant. |
| API key/OAuth2 → none | Preserve both record IDs and association; clear incompatible canonical auth configuration and remove the global grant in the existing transaction. |
| none → API key | Require a usable new key; create/replace the canonical global grant. |
| Edit API key without replacing key | Preserve the existing usable grant; an empty password field is not a request to clear it or choose no-auth. |
| none/API key → OAuth2 | Use the established OAuth setup/attempt lifecycle, preserving setup-pending and discovery rules. |
| Auth change with active personal grants | Preserve `:incompatible_live_grants`; show an actionable error and leave both records unchanged. Do not automatically delete people's grants. |
| Edit provider/endpoint/name only | Preserve canonical auth mode, configuration, and grant. |
| Repeat no-auth save | Idempotent canonical state; no new credential or grant. |

No-auth runtime resolution returns empty authentication. Outbound AI requests must not synthesize an empty bearer/API-key header. Existing revoked/expired grant history remains governed by Connect's cleanup policy; it must not become usable after a mode change.

## Implementation sequence

This approved plan is now materialized in the child issues below. Use one issue per step, with additional splits if ownership or validation warrants them. Prefix titles with their assigned issue IDs. A simple sequential graph avoids unnecessary dependency diamonds:

```mermaid
graph LR
  A[1 Canonical contract] --> B[2 Migration compatibility]
  B --> C[3 Auth Credential form]
  C --> D[4 AI form and writers]
  D --> E[5 Metadata retirement and integration]
  E --> F[6 Human UX approval]
  F --> G[7 Feature E2E]
  G --> H[8 Review coverage and final validation]
```

### 1. Make canonical mode explicit in the domain contract

**Files:** `lib/zaq/system.ex`, `lib/zaq/system/ai_provider_credential.ex`, `lib/zaq/system/ai_provider_credential_configuration.ex`; relevant Connect context/mutation/credential modules and Engine event contracts as needed.

**Work:**
- Read owning module docs before changes. Add the explicit input/virtual projection described above; project secret-free canonical state for AI list/get/change operations without per-row query proliferation.
- Replace AI metadata-based mode inference. Keep unrelated edits from overwriting canonical OAuth settings with stale AI metadata.
- Centralize no-auth transition normalization in the existing Connect configuration operation so both forms use the same behavior. Clear all incompatible secret/configuration fields required by current schema constraints, set disabled policy/configuration binding, and remove the org grant.
- Preserve locking, authorization, rollback, encryption, mutation events, and invalidation. Validate linked-AI mode/provider restrictions on either write path.
- Refresh canonical state on subsequent loads/edits. A stale AI form must not silently restore the old mode after a direct Auth Credential edit; use explicit-change tracking or the existing stale-write protection contract, with a reproducing test.

**Tests first / branches:** Extend `test/zaq/system/ai_provider_credential_test.exs`, `ai_provider_credential_transaction_test.exs`, and relevant Connect mutation/credential tests. Cover each transition above, invalid modes, atom/string request keys, omitted mode, existing key preservation, active personal-grant rejection, linked-provider restrictions, stale edits, and transaction rollback when either side fails.

**Mocking:** Real SQL sandbox and real Connect mutations; fake only an external OAuth/token endpoint where needed. No broad success stubs around the operation under test.

**Documentation:** Update module contracts immediately; consolidate service guidance in step 5.

**Action reuse:** Extend System's existing configuration adapter and Connect's existing transactional operation. Inputs are administrator-authorized configuration plus an explicit mode; outputs/errors retain the established result shapes, including changeset/configuration errors and incompatible grants. Consumers are BO and provisioning via existing Engine events; BO keeps `NodeRouter.dispatch/1` with `%Zaq.Event{}` and trusted actor context. No new Action/tool is needed for this cohesive configuration capability. Tests must demonstrate both entry points share Connect mutations and preserve IDs/events.

### 2. Fix preflight and actual legacy backfill together

**Files:** `lib/zaq/system/ai_provider_credential_migration.ex`, `priv/repo/migrations/20260918131000_backfill_connect_backed_ai_credentials.exs`, their existing migration tests.

**Classification contract:**
- Already-associated rows stay associated and retain canonical mode; never reinterpret their retained legacy key.
- Exactly one valid legacy OAuth org grant follows the existing OAuth migration path.
- Multiple/incompatible legacy grants remain blocked.
- Legacy API-key/default-mode entries with no OAuth intent and a NULL, empty, whitespace-only, or successfully decrypted blank key classify as no-auth.
- A readable nonblank key remains API key. Do not trim/change an actual key's value while classifying it.
- Unreadable encrypted material remains an error, never no-auth.
- Explicit legacy no-auth remains accepted when its data is consistent. Contradictory declarations/material must not produce mismatched mode/binding.
- Explicit OAuth intent, OAuth-only provider/profile, or incomplete OAuth setup without its grant must not be converted to no-auth just because its key is blank.
- Missing metadata can represent the old default API-key mode; malformed/unknown metadata is not blanket permission to reinterpret an entry. Define and test these cases separately.

**Work:**
- Run classification against a stable migration snapshot/appropriate locks. Ensure locking actually executes before classification; queued Ecto migration SQL is not automatically executed before an immediate Repo query.
- Feed the same classification into canonical credential creation, binding selection, and grant insertion. A migration-local, transaction-scoped staging table containing only AI IDs, classification, and source IDs is an acceptable way to bridge Elixir decryption/classification and SQL. Do not reimplement blank-value classification in SQL over ciphertext.
- Keep preflight output bounded and secret-free. Retain ciphertext only where existing rollback policy requires it; never persist/log decrypted blank/key values in migration staging.
- No-auth gets no org grant; valid API-key ciphertext is copied through the established path; OAuth copy/cleanup follows the current tested contract.
- Maintain restartability and association uniqueness; abort atomically on blockers.
- Edit the failing historical migration because later migrations cannot unblock it. Already-upgraded installations will use the later cleanup migration in step 5.

**Tests first / branches:** Extend `ai_provider_credential_migration_test.exs` and `ai_provider_credential_backfill_migration_test.exs`. Exercise actual migration up/down/up with absent/blank/encrypted-blank keys, valid encrypted keys, unreadable ciphertext, explicit no-auth, incomplete OAuth, valid OAuth, ambiguous grants, mixed datasets, already-associated rows, and reruns. Assert canonical mode/binding/policy, grant counts, retained ciphertext, association IDs, and rollback behavior—not only classifier output. Add properties over supported whitespace/key input spaces and verify classification/backfill agreement.

**Mocking:** Isolated migration database/schema using the existing test harness; real encryption with isolated test configuration. No external services.

**Documentation:** Update preflight/migration module docs. Verify current rollback source behavior against code/tests: existing service prose and migration source observed earlier do not fully agree about retaining legacy OAuth rows.

**Action reuse:** Extend the existing migration classifier/backfill locally. This is one-time schema/data upgrade work requiring old table shapes and migration locks, not an independently exposed runtime Action. Verify classification and persistence agreement and deterministic retries.

### 3. Expose no-auth on Auth Credentials

**Files:** `lib/zaq_web/components/connect_credential_form.ex`, `lib/zaq_web/live/bo/system/system_config/connect_helpers.ex`, `connect_credentials_tab.ex`, relevant handlers in `system_config_live.ex`.

**Work:**
- Add a human-readable **No authentication** option while retaining existing modes, including JWT bearer for eligible generic credentials.
- Hide auth secret, OAuth, JWT, scope, personal-policy, and request-format controls that do not apply to no-auth. Show concise text explaining that requests carry no authentication.
- Normalize selection through the shared configuration path. Hidden or stale submitted fields cannot retain incompatible configuration or bypass domain validation.
- Show no-auth as a valid configured state, not a missing/expired grant. Surface linked-AI restrictions and personal-grant conflicts clearly.
- Refresh associated AI projections after save through existing loading/invalidation mechanisms.
- Reuse the existing form/design-system components and bundled assets; follow the design skill/approval rules before applying UI changes.

**Tests first / branches:** Extend `test/zaq_web/components/connect_credential_form_test.exs` and `test/zaq_web/live/bo/system/system_config/connect_credential_events_test.exs`. Cover selectable mode, conditional controls, persisted edits, forged/stale fields, error display, JWT regression, and canonical state reflected on the AI side.

**Mocking:** Component tests for rendering; real domain integration in LiveView tests, with only external OAuth boundaries faked.

**Documentation:** Form/helper docs where behavior changes; service/UI instructions in step 5.

**Action reuse:** Reuse the existing BO event and shared Connect mutation from step 1. UI normalization is local presentation logic, not a new Action. Verify authorization and shared persistence through request-to-database tests.

### 4. Wire AI Credentials and every current AI writer to canonical mode

**Files:** `lib/zaq_web/live/bo/system/system_config/ai_credentials_tab.ex`, `ai_credential_events.ex`, `system_config_live.ex`, `lib/zaq/user_portal/provisioner.ex`, relevant seeds/fixtures and callers discovered by the writer audit.

**Work:**
- Offer **API key**, **OAuth2**, and **No authentication** using explicit form state populated from the canonical credential.
- Translate AI mode changes into updates of that same Auth Credential. Persist no duplicate mode in AI metadata.
- Hide irrelevant controls for no-auth and render the correct list/detail label and configured status even without a grant.
- Replace OAuth gating and profile-based mode inference with canonical mode checks. Preserve OAuth behavior selection on the Connect credential and the existing pending-setup lifecycle.
- Remove old help text claiming API keys always override the selected mode. Explain blank-key preservation on edit and require a usable key for a new API-key setup.
- Convert provisioning, seed, and fixture writes to explicit modes. A deliberately keyless provisioning path must send `none`, not rely on a blank key or old metadata marker.
- Confirm both forms refresh/reopen consistently after edits through either entry point.

**Tests first / branches:** Extend AI events/tab tests, the relevant SystemConfigLive integration tests, and provisioning tests. Cover create/save/reopen for all modes, all supported transitions, direct Auth edits reflected in AI, AI edits reflected in Auth, metadata attempts to override mode, key-preserving edits, provider-only edits, Codex OAuth behavior, and unauthorized requests.

**Mocking:** SQL sandbox and real domain operations. Stub only remote OAuth/provider communication.

**Documentation:** Update form/event API comments and relevant provisioning contract docs. No new agent tool or workflow entry point.

**Action reuse:** Extend the existing AI configuration consumer and reuse Engine dispatch/System/Connect operations. Keep provisioning on its existing authorized event boundary. Verify both UI and provisioning paths obey the same explicit-mode contract.

### 5. Retire AI metadata mode and prove upgrade/runtime integration

**Files:** A new forward migration under `priv/repo/migrations/` with the implementation-time timestamp; System/Engine consumers identified by a bounded audit; `docs/services/system-config.md` and relevant existing operator guide(s).

**Work:**
- Remove the obsolete AI `auth_kind` metadata key from associated rows after canonical backfill, including databases where the earlier migration already succeeded. Preserve unrelated metadata and existing OAuth setup bookkeeping needed by the current lifecycle.
- Do not change canonical mode based on retained AI API keys or stale metadata on already-associated rows. No extra persisted auth-mode field or permanent runtime fallback.
- Before removing legacy keys, verify needed OAuth configuration is already canonical; do not broadly delete authentication-related metadata without auditing its consumers.
- Make cleanup retry-safe. Its down path can reconstruct the legacy mode marker from canonical auth kind where needed for the supported rollback chain; preserve existing rollback refusal rules for personal state. Test no-auth down/up after cleanup and after editing through either form.
- Audit runtime, UI, provisioning, tests, fixtures, and active docs for AI mode reads/writes through metadata. Remaining interpretation must be clearly migration/rollback-only; ordinary Connect metadata such as `auth_profile` retains its legitimate purpose.
- Verify AI runtime no-auth resolution and outbound request construction. Test pending OAuth completion/refresh after a switch to no-auth; stale work must not restore an old mode or grant. Extend existing attempt invalidation/mutation handling only if the regression test exposes a gap.
- Update authoritative docs to describe canonical ownership, the one-time legacy-empty-key rule, future explicit selection, transition errors, and supported upgrade/rollback behavior. Correct discovered stale rollout prose against tested source behavior.

**Tests first / branches:** Add a cleanup migration test and extend `test/zaq/engine/connect/ai_runtime_credentials_test.exs`, relevant resolver/mutation/OAuth-attempt tests, and the AI transport boundary test appropriate to the actual consumer. Cover both previously blocked and already-successful rollout paths, metadata absence/conflicts, no-auth request headers, stale OAuth work, rollback guards, and unrelated metadata preservation.

**Mocking:** Real database/mutation behavior; local request capture or existing injected transport at the network edge. No live provider requests or leaked credentials.

**Action reuse:** Cleanup stays migration-local. Runtime continues to reuse the existing resolver and mutation/invalidation machinery. No new resolver, auth system, or Action is introduced. Documentation-only portions are not applicable to Action reuse.

### 6. Obtain human UX/UI approval

Demonstrate both forms and the linked-record interaction using the existing browser workflow. Include no-auth creation, switching an existing AI entry, direct Auth Credential edits reflected in AI, validation errors, and the personal-grant restriction. Record approval against this final implemented scope in Beadwork.

New feature E2E authoring remains blocked until that approval. Immediate unit, integration, property, and LiveView tests in steps 1–5 are not deferred. Existing required E2E continues to run during implementation.

Action reuse: not applicable; this is a review gate.

### 7. Add the consolidated feature E2E coverage

Use the existing system-config E2E suite after approval. One tracked issue covers:
- Create a keyless AI configuration and verify its associated Auth Credential is no-auth.
- Edit mode from either form and verify the other reflects it after refresh/reopen.
- Verify API-key creation validation and saved-key preservation on edit.
- Verify no-auth controls/status and OAuth-only provider restrictions.
- Verify a representative no-auth request through a controlled local endpoint if supported by the existing harness; keep lower-level header assertions regardless.

Use deterministic fixtures and no real OAuth/provider services. Keep scenario descriptions current throughout implementation, then author against the approved final UI.

Action reuse: reuse existing test bootstrap and system-config journeys; no production operation added. Record final E2E results in the issue/PR.

### 8. Review, coverage, and final validation

- After each implementation issue: run `mix q` through Context Mode, then the relevant isolated tests; review the diff and Action reuse evidence. Fix failures before closing the issue.
- Run existing system-config E2E as required by `docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md`; after approval also run the consolidated new coverage. Report environment blockers explicitly.
- Review secret-free projections/logging, lock order, stale reads, linked-provider restrictions, runtime metadata retirement, rollback, and fresh/previously-migrated database paths.
- After implementation and PR review approval, perform the repository's coverage handoff. Generate fresh coverage with the prescribed timeout, address findings, and revalidate any changes.
- Run final `mix precommit` through Context Mode with the prescribed 900,000 ms timeout before requesting final human approval. Repeat after subsequent changes.
- Commit/push/PR/merge actions require their normal authorization; this plan does not authorize them.

Action reuse: review/validation only; no additional production operation.

## Completion criteria

1. Both forms expose No authentication and persist the same canonical mode.
2. AI form changes preserve the underlying Auth Credential ID and update it transactionally.
3. Eligible legacy empty-key entries migrate successfully, including encrypted blanks, while corrupt secrets and invalid OAuth remain errors.
4. Preflight and actual SQL backfill agree on mode, binding, and grant creation.
5. Already-upgraded installations receive metadata cleanup without changing canonical authentication.
6. No ongoing AI runtime, UI, or writer depends on `metadata["auth_kind"]` or infers mode from OAuth profile/retained legacy keys.
7. No-auth is secret-free, has disabled personal policy, has no usable grant, and sends no authentication headers.
8. Both entry points enforce the same provider/association restrictions and personal-grant transition guard.
9. Existing API-key/OAuth behavior, key-preserving edits, provisioning, retries, and supported rollback paths pass regression coverage.
10. Documentation, human UX approval, required E2E, coverage review, and final validation are complete and recorded before final sign-off.


## Executable issue graph
- zaq-gmx.1: Extend canonical Connect no-auth transitions and linked-AI guards
- zaq-gmx.2: Make AI configuration mode explicit and project canonical state
- zaq-gmx.3: Align legacy empty-key preflight and Connect backfill
- zaq-gmx.4: Expose No authentication in Auth Credential form
- zaq-gmx.5: Use canonical auth mode in AI form and provisioning writers
- zaq-gmx.6: Clean up legacy AI auth metadata with reversible migration
- zaq-gmx.7: Verify canonical AI runtime cutover and document no-auth contract
- zaq-gmx.8: Obtain human approval of final no-auth credential UX
- zaq-gmx.9: Add approved no-auth credential E2E journeys
- zaq-gmx.10: Complete no-auth review coverage and final validation

```mermaid
graph LR
  zaq_gmx_1["zaq-gmx.1"] --> zaq_gmx_2["zaq-gmx.2"]
  zaq_gmx_2["zaq-gmx.2"] --> zaq_gmx_3["zaq-gmx.3"]
  zaq_gmx_3["zaq-gmx.3"] --> zaq_gmx_4["zaq-gmx.4"]
  zaq_gmx_4["zaq-gmx.4"] --> zaq_gmx_5["zaq-gmx.5"]
  zaq_gmx_5["zaq-gmx.5"] --> zaq_gmx_6["zaq-gmx.6"]
  zaq_gmx_6["zaq-gmx.6"] --> zaq_gmx_7["zaq-gmx.7"]
  zaq_gmx_7["zaq-gmx.7"] --> zaq_gmx_8["zaq-gmx.8"]
  zaq_gmx_8["zaq-gmx.8"] --> zaq_gmx_9["zaq-gmx.9"]
  zaq_gmx_9["zaq-gmx.9"] --> zaq_gmx_10["zaq-gmx.10"]
```

Dependency rationale: a linear chain intentionally prioritizes safe review over parallelism. Connect domain precedes System contract; migration classification precedes consumer exposure; both forms/writers precede metadata retirement; integration precedes final UX approval, E2E and final validation. Split steps 1 and 5 have distinct owning domains/test surfaces. Only zaq-gmx.1 should be an unblocked implementation root.

## Existing issue reconciliation
Corrective follow-up to zaq-jrg.23/.24/.25/.26/.28 and completed zaq-p9l.4/.5. Do not repeat initial association/schema rollout or reopen closed historical work. Preserve unrelated scope and existing statuses. This plan replaces only the legacy-empty-key rejection policy and metadata-based mode ownership for this fix; runtime writes stay explicit. Plan approval is not implemented UX approval.

Canonical Connect no-auth transition + linked-AI guards; explicit AI auth_kind and canonical projection; legacy keyless preflight/backfill agreement; both BO forms; metadata retirement migration and provisioning writers; system-config docs/Storybook. Validation: mix q passed; mix test test/zaq/system test/zaq/engine/connect test/zaq_web/live/bo/system test/zaq_web/components/connect_credential_form_test.exs test/zaq/user_portal => 1190 tests, 29 properties, 0 failures; existing system-config Firefox E2E => 55 passed.
